ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended by Law No. 8 of 2023; Prime Ministerial Decree No. 216 of 2002 (Executive Regulations of Law No. 80 of 2002); Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law) and Law No. 72 of 2017 (Investment Law), as administered by GAFI; GAFI/Commercial Registry circulars on disclosure of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and national AML/CFT obligations issued by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) and Central Bank of Egypt (CBE).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Companies Registry or notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for contracting states) or Egyptian Consular Legalization at the Embassy/Consulate of Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or corporate secretary of the originating company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin, with subsequent Egyptian MFA legalization if executed abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian Consular Legalization + registration before an Egyptian notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports of each UBO, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authority or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and source-of-wealth letter for each UBO (for AML/EDD file)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chartered bank maintaining the UBO's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization / Apostille, if required by the designated non-financial business or profession

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT compliance declaration and sanctions-screening statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign counsel or notary in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Apostille or Egyptian Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and authorized representatives against United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK OFSI/HMT list, Egypt's competent authority terrorist list, and INTERPOL notifications. PEP status is determined for current senior public officials, their family members, close associates, and former PEPs for at least 12 months after leaving office. Any measured risk above Low triggers Enhanced Due Diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, corroborated evidence of beneficial ownership, and senior-management approval. The CMRA scope with Stripe and credit-card payment rails is classified under the AML risk tier as Medium_Risk_Enhanced; no business relationship may be formed unless the UBO files contain a verified legal-person ownership chain down to natural persons.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop Shop / Investor Center and Commercial Registry electronic portal (services.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All applications and the legal name must be recorded in Arabic. A foreign-language name may be included as an additional name, but the Arabic transliteration is controlling. The transliteration must be phonetically faithful, must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name in the Commercial Registry, and must not imply a licensed banking, insurance, securities, defense, military, or public-sector activity unless the relevant ministerial no-objection certificate is obtained. Arabic script spelling errors or misleading transliteration are grounds for rejection.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: any expression contrary to public order, morality, or Islamic Sharia principles
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name shall be re-submitted only after remedying the notified ground of refusal. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Commercial Registry Assessment Committee within 15 working days of the rejection notice, attaching the original rejection, corrected Arabic transliteration, and any ministerial no-objection letter. If GAFI maintains the rejection, the applicant may initiate judicial annulment proceedings before the Egyptian Administrative Court (State Council) within 60 days of the final administrative decision, with simultaneous indication of alternative names to avoid delay. Extension of a valid name reservation is only by a fresh GAFI resubmission before expiry of the 30-day window; no statutory extension after expiry is recognized.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this CMRA/digital mail-scanning activity when the registered office is a licensed Egyptian provider maintaining a physical address in Egypt, an authorized local agent, and actual mail-scanning equipment/location. A P.O. Box address or mail-forwarding-only arrangement is not sufficient. The provider may serve as the registered office, but the LLC must have a verifiable office capacity to receive regulatory notices, tax authority visits, and service of process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated. There is an estimated 70-80% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first 18 months, because GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit treat virtual-office/CMRA registrations with overseas UBOs and card-based payment rails as Medium_Risk_Enhanced and therefore subject to discretionary site visits to verify personnel, server/mail facilities, and commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law) as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009; Law No. 72 of 2017 (Investment Law) – LLC provisions at Articles 42–67 of the Companies Law; Investment Law Articles 1–26.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investor Services Center (One-Stop Shop); Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association (Aqd Al-Ta’sees) and Notarized Articles of Association; Commercial Registration Application (Form 'Qad El-Sijill').
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law 159/1981 and Investment Law 72/2017; the capital is fixed by the memorandum of association. Cash capital contributions must be deposited in an Egyptian bank account in the company’s name and held in escrow until the Commercial Registration Certificate is issued; the bank's capital deposit certificate is submitted to GAFI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the Memorandum of Association filed with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) is hereby adopted. 2. That each founding member shall subscribe to the shares set opposite their name in the capital schedule of the Memorandum, and the entire issued share capital is deemed subscribed. 3. That the registered office located at [Virtual Office Address, Egypt] is approved and adopted for the service of statutory notices and tax correspondence. 4. That the following officers are appointed for the first term: [Full Name], General Manager; [Full Name], Chief Financial Officer; [Full Name], Corporate Secretary. 5. That the appointed officers are jointly authorized to open bank accounts, sign tax returns, and make all regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Verify Activity Classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Name Reservation Window (online portal: www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation application via GAFI’s electronic portal, listing three fallback trade names. Attach a short description of the CMRA and digital-scanning activity. GAFI’s legal examiner verifies name uniqueness, Arabic/English transliteration, and compatibility with ISIC 8299. Upon approval, obtain the provisional name certificate valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Copy of founding members’ valid passports or national IDs
Civil information extract for each manager (if Egyptian)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit a written response with alternative names within 15 working days; GAFI may reroute the file to the Commercial Registry screening. The name reservation fee is credited or refunded for amended names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Review, and Notarize Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Clerk of Civil Status / Notariat) and GAFI Pre-Incorporation Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage an Egyptian attorney or notary to draft the Arabic Memorandum of Association (Aqd Al-Ta’sees) in accordance with Articles 42–67 of Law 159/1981. The MOA must specify: company name, registered office, purpose, capital, share allocation, management rules, and duration. All founding members sign before a public notary, who authenticates the signatures. Submit the draft to GAFI’s legal department for pre-review or file directly if using an approved notary.
required_dossiers: Passports or national IDs of all members
Registered office lease or virtual office service agreement
Statement of bank capital deposit (if cash capital)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or GAFI legal comments on the MOA, amend the relevant clauses through a supplementary deed and restart notarization; no new name fee is incurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Company Bank Account and Deposit Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in Egypt (e.g., NBE, CIB, Alex Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After MOA draft approval, sign the corporate account opening application at the chosen bank and submit the notarized MOA and name certificate. Deposit the stated paid-up capital (if any) into a temporary company account. The bank issues a capital deposit certificate (Shahadat Iidna') indicating the amount and account number; this certificate is required for GAFI lodgment. For LLCs with no cash capital, the bank may issue a nil-balance letter if the physical or virtual office is duly confirmed.
required_dossiers: Passports or national IDs of signatories
Utility bill or virtual office document evidencing premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application for KYC deficiencies, submit supplementary identification and the corporate beneficial ownership declaration; a second bank may be selected within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Documents with GAFI and Obtain Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Company Incorporation Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized MOA, name certificate, capital deposit certificate, registered office proof, and all member identification forms to the GAFI incorporation officer. GAFI reviews the application, collects statutory filing fees and stamp duties, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Commercial Registration Certificate in one workflow. This step is integrated with the Tax Authority and Social Insurance Office through GAFI’s single-counter interface.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises queries, remedy them within 30 days by submitting corrected documents or paying any late-lodgment fee. After issuance, correct any typographical errors in the Commercial Register via a rectification application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax, VAT, Payroll, and Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Social Insurance Authority (NSSA), via GAFI e-notification or direct windows
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Commercial Registration Certificate, file Tax Form No. 1 with the competent Tax Office to obtain the Tax Card and VAT registration (if expected turnover exceeds EGP 500,000). Register employees with NSSA within 14 days of payroll commencement. Upload the Commercial Registration Certificate and MOA to ETA’s portal or visit the tax office; pay the nominal certificate issuance fee and obtain the corporate tax ID (NIF) and payroll number.
required_dossiers: Tenancy contract or virtual office service contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA rejects the registration for mismatch of address or activity, correct the registered office and purpose with GAFI and resubmit Form 1. Late-registration penalties are waived if the one-stop-shop processing chain is substantiated by GAFI documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Internal Trade Development Authority (ITDA) and the Governorate Commercial Licensing Directorate (Rakhis Mahal)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial License for Business Services – Virtual Office and Correspondence Scanning (Rukhsa Tijariah Noqatiyah)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Exempt) – Minimal environmental footprint; no EIA report required; mandatory registration under the Waste Management Law (Law 202/2020) for handling shredded paper and electronic records.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater discharge; VOCs not applicable. Electronic and paper waste must be segregated and transferred to EEAA-licensed recyclers. Storage and disposal shall comply with EEAA limits for commercial solid waste and end-of-life electronic equipment under Law 4/1994 and its executive regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Civil Defense Authority for the licensed premises; structural load confirmation from the building owner; occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower under Law No. 12 of 2003; workplace approval for installed digital communication and mail-handling equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; official portal: eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-receipt clearance portal: invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Egyptian LLC: complete incorporation with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and obtain the Commercial Registry extract; file the corporate tax registration application with the competent ETA office within 30 days of commercial registration; receive the Tax Card containing the TIN and corporate tax file number; apply separately for VAT registration where annual taxable supplies reach or are expected to reach EGP 500,000; then activate the ETA e-invoicing dashboard and complete ETA API integration before issuing compliant invoices. The TIN must appear in all commercial, customs, and electronic invoicing records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable. An Egyptian LLC is treated as a per-se corporation and is not eligible for pass-through or check-the-box treatment. Egypt does not recognize hybrid mismatch elections or domestic fiscal unity elections for LLCs; entity classification can only be changed by altering the legal form of incorporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Egyptian Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, and its Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable supplies of goods and/or services during a 12-month period; non-resident taxable persons with an Egyptian taxable establishment apply the same threshold, while non-residents supplying specified digital or services with in-country use may have reverse-charge or registration obligations irrespective of the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory ETA e-invoicing and phased e-receipt regime. Registered taxpayers must generate invoices in XML/JSON and transmit them through the official ETA API for near-real-time validation. Each approved invoice receives an ETA-validated QR code, unique document number, and digital stamp; unvalidated invoices are non-compliant for input VAT deduction and may trigger administrative penalties. Fiscal clearance is performed electronically, and no non-digital invoice may be issued by a covered taxpayer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported to a non-resident under a valid customs export declaration, and to services supplied from Egypt to a non-resident where the place of supply and effective use and enjoyment are outside Egypt. The taxpayer must be VAT-registered, flag the relevant e-invoice as zero-rated, report the export transaction in the periodic VAT return, and preserve documentary proof of export and receipt of foreign currency proceeds in Egypt. Offshore email scanning, mail forwarding, and virtual-office administrative services may qualify where the recipient is foreign, the output is delivered outside Egypt, and the service is not consumed in-country.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (final/approved export discharge) for tangible goods and physical mail items
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or postal export receipt proving physical dispatch from Egypt to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an Egyptian licensed bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in Egypt within the prescribed repatriation period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA cross-matches zero-rated VAT returns, e-invoices, customs declarations, and bank remittance records. Missing, contradictory, or false substantiation results in reassessment at 14% VAT, reversal of any claimed refund, late-payment interest, administrative fines, and potential tax-evasion prosecution with criminal penalties extending to the legal representative. Retrospective clawback may apply from the date the zero-rating was originally claimed, and the exporter may also lose customs facilitation status and face suspension of future zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) and its Foreign Exchange Control Unit pursuant to Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) and CBE AML/CFT regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains current account convertibility under IMF Article VIII, with the Egyptian pound (EGP) traded in a managed-float interbank market. Capital account transactions remain restricted: inbound direct equity investment must be routed through a CBE-licensed bank with GAFI registration, while outbound dividend remittances require tax clearance certificates, CBE-approved purpose codes, and verified underlying documents. For a non-resident-owned LLC engaged in virtual office and scanning services, profit repatriation is lawful after corporate tax, VAT, and stamp tax compliance; the CBE applies enhanced scrutiny to foreign currency transfers exceeding intraday transaction thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE circulars issued pursuant to Law No. 194 of 2020, export proceeds must be fully repatriated to an Egyptian bank account within the commonly imposed timeline of 90 days from the date of shipment or negotiation of the exporting documents; CBE may temporarily reduce the window to 30 days during liquidity-stress periods. As of the current policy, there is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio of export proceeds into EGP; exporters may retain foreign currency in CBE-licensed bank accounts and convert at the prevailing interbank market rate, subject to banks' monitoring and reporting obligations. Failure to meet the repatriation timeline triggers CBE penalties, bank account restrictions, and loss of access to import finance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI and non-CBE-licensed payment institutions have low viability as a primary corporate treasury rail. Egyptian law requires all EGP deposits and clearing activity to be conducted through licensed banks or licensed fintech entities operating under CBE sandbox or Payment Systems Law (Law No. 18 of 2019). Foreign EMIs are not recognized as banks and cannot provide statutory corporate bank accounts, foreign exchange services, or CBE reporting. Their use is limited to ancillary card-issuing functions integrated with a CBE-licensed bank sponsor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The CBE and Egyptian AML/CFT rules mandate an in-person KYC interview for corporate account opening involving foreign shareholders. At least one natural-person beneficial owner or a legally authorised director must appear physically before a bank officer, presenting the original corporate documents, passports, power of attorney, and ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) declarations. Some tier-1 banks allow remote video verification for supplementary signatories after physical onboarding, but the initial identification of the legal representative and UBO is almost always done in-branch. The virtual-office nature of the business does not waive these requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company and post-box corporate structure indicators arising from the use of a virtual office with no physical staff or standalone premises.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the fully notarized LLC incorporation package from the Egyptian Companies Registry; a valid commercial register extract; a valid tax card and social insurance registration; a CBE beneficial-owner disclosure form; a signed virtual-office lease with a reputable Egyptian service provider; physical presence evidence of at least one local compliance officer or full-time employee carrying out scanning and mail-forwarding operations; and a list of third-party clients with underlying service agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign capital injections from a jurisdiction perceived as high-risk or unexplained source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit corporate resolutions of the foreign shareholder(s) authorizing the capital injection; notarized and apostilled board minutes or powers of attorney; bank statements of the remitting entity covering the last six months; clear source-of-funds narrative and supporting invoices or subscription agreements; and a UBO declaration demonstrating no sanctions exposure or political-exposure match. A sworn affidavit on the absence of illegal funds may be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-lite but high transaction frequency and international remittances for mail-scanning subscriptions, potentially indicating third-party payment laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a granular KYC file for every merchant/mail receiving customer, including beneficial ownership and passport scans; provide a detailed AML risk matrix and transaction-size rationale; disclose expected monthly volumes and payment rails (Stripe recurring, credit cards); and implement a documented compliance policy for rejecting third-party payments and reporting suspicious transactions to the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The LLC's inbound equity capital must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the designated CBE-licensed bank, with the CBE Foreign Exchange Manual purpose code for capital contribution (commonly 'P010' or equivalent) and a clear remittance narrative referencing the shareholders' subscription resolution. The receiving bank will issue a Foreign Investment Deposit Certificate and register the inflow with the CBE; where applicable, the LLC must also register the investment with GAFI. The bank will require the original capital subscription, proof of UBO, and an undertaking to use the funds for the registered business scope only.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operating disbursements (scanning equipment imports, software license fees, agent commissions, and vendor payments) are settled through SWIFT MT103 payment orders supported by CBE purpose codes, commercial invoices, contracts, and, where applicable, supplier e-KYC files. For high-value or economically sensitive payments, the bank may request a CBE clearance certificate, tax card verification, and trade documents. Letters of credit (documentary credit) are available for imported capital equipment, but are not generally required for service-based disbursements; MT103 remains the primary clearing rail due to speed and simplicity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts (onshore, with genuine commercial underlying and collateral, typically up to 12 months)
Cross-currency swaps between EGP and major foreign currencies executed with a CBE-licensed bank
Spot foreign exchange contracts at the interbank market rate
Currency options (subject to CBE eligibility and strictly tied to real trade or investment exposure)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the tax year-end; calendar-year LLCs due by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty and 0.5% monthly surcharge on unpaid tax; continued default triggers enforced assessment, suspension of tax clearance certificate, and restriction of commercial activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax periodic returns and annual VAT reconciliation declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT returns due by the end of the following month; annual reconciliation due by 31 January after the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-return fines scaled by ETA, monthly late-payment interest, temporary suspension of VAT registration certificate, and collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / AML Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for the preceding calendar year; UBO changes filed within 30 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative daily penalties for late confirmation; repeated non-compliance can suspend registry extracts and lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registration renewal and economic activity license renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry under GAFI and the competent District Economic Activity Licensing Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal filed at least 30 days before license anniversary and no later than 31 March for calendar-year licenses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License file archived, unlicensed operations prohibited, daily fines imposed, and persistent non-renewal triggers administrative de-registration and strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory for every active LLC because the corporate tax regime requires an auditor's report to accompany the annual return; dormant LLCs filing a nil declaration may be exempt. Banking, insurance, brokerage, and GAFI-licensed investment entities are always subject to independent statutory audit regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially aligned with IFRS; banks, insurance companies, and non-bank financial institutions follow sector-specific presentation requirements of CBE and the Financial Regulatory Authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The manager must identify and verify the ultimate beneficial owner at onboarding and on every quotaholder change. The UBO record is re-confirmed at the annual general meeting within 3 months of year-end and the confirmation is filed with GAFI by 31 March. A quota/share transfer is recognized only after the transferee is recorded in the Register of Members and the UBO register is updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Meetings and Managerial Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 – USD 480 per annum for registered office and licensed corporate agent services, depending on scanning volume and mail volume
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 400 – USD 1,200 for a small LLC engaged in virtual-office and mail-scanning services; USD 150 – USD 300 additional if ETA compliance review or archival reconstruction is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate income tax rate of 22.5% under Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 as amended by Law No. 51/2023. No general tax concession applies to ISIC 8299 CMRA or mail-scanning services. Investment Law No. 72/2017 permits a five-year tax holiday or 50% taxable-profit deduction for qualifying projects in less-developed governorates or the Suez Canal Economic Zone, but a standalone virtual-office and mail-scanning entity will not ordinarily satisfy the labor and industrial investment criteria. Cross-border card-rail revenue such as Stripe recurring subscription fees is fully taxable as Egyptian-source and worldwide income of the resident LLC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 3 (Corporate Profit Tax Declaration) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg, supported by CIC commercial-register credentials and mandatory e-invoice/e-receipt integration for issued CMRA invoices.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual: one definitive return per 12-month fiscal year; quarterly provisional CIT instalments are remitted separately through the ETA portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed and the full tax paid within four months after the fiscal year-end; a calendar-year LLC must file by 30 April of the following year. Extensions apply only with ETA pre-approval and do not suspend interest accrual.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Egyptian Tax Identification Number (TIN) of the LLC, cross-referenced to the Commercial Registration certificate and the establishment license of the virtual-office mail-scanning activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this return themselves; the Egyptian LLC files as a resident juridical person and must disclose foreign direct or indirect ownership in the ownership annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 - Gross receipts from all activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide gross revenue including virtual-office subscription fees, mail scanning fees, digital forwarding charges, and Stripe recurring card payments, net of refunds and chargebacks; foreign-currency receipts are translated to EGP at the Central Bank of Egypt exchange rate on the transaction date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parents cannot net out cross-border platform fees without an arm's-length TP study; all foreign revenue must be declared with supporting payment-rail reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs include licensed office rent, salaries, mail-scanner software, courier and logistics charges, depreciation, insurance, and service fees supported by valid e-invoices; expenses lacking documentation are disallowed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, software royalties, or technical fees paid to a foreign related party are deductible only when supported by contracts, proven services, and evidence of 20% Egyptian withholding or a treaty exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 12 - Net taxable income and loss carry-forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after statutory adjustments and application of available tax losses carried forward within the five-year limit from prior tax years; no loss carry-back is permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses cannot be transferred from the foreign shareholder into the Egyptian LLC; the loss utilization schedule must be attached to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 20 - Total tax credits and final CIT payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregation of quarterly provisional instalments, foreign tax credits for treaty countries, and withholding-credit balances, followed by application of the 22.5% statutory rate and computation of the balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders must be cross-referenced in the WHT annex, and the 10% dividend distribution tax must be declared and paid by the LLC before remittance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a progressive fine of EGP 1,000 to EGP 20,000 plus an additional tax of 2% per month or fraction on the unpaid CIT. Late payment incurs the same 2% monthly surcharge with automatic ETA collection, bank garnishment, and suspension of tax clearance certificates. Persistent non-filing may result in deemed assessment and criminal referral.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Provisional CIT Instalment Voucher generated in the ETA e-portal in accordance with the advance-payment obligation for juridical persons.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly: four instalments per fiscal year, each approximating 25% of the prior-year assessed tax base or 90% of the estimated current-year liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are due by 30 April, 31 July, 31 October, and 31 January for calendar-year taxpayers, corresponding to the month following each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: QRTR-Box 1 - Instalment period and tax base indicator
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the quarter reference period and the provisional computation basis selected by the LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no direct instalment obligation, but the LLC must fund instalments from operating cash flow before effecting external dividend distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment of quarterly instalments is subject to the 2% monthly additional tax on the shortfall, and repeated missed instalments trigger ETA enforcement action against the LLC's bank accounts and administrative attachment of the licensed office equipment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends and profit distributions paid by an Egyptian LLC to both resident and non-resident shareholders, imposed under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005; no further Egyptian taxation applies to a non-resident recipient, but treaty rates may reduce the 10% rate to 5% to 15% depending on shareholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home-tax authority and submit a treaty-relief application to the ETA International Taxation Unit prior to distribution, together with proof of beneficial ownership, shareholding percentage, and substance documentation. Upon approval, the LLC withholds at the treaty rate; if 10% was withheld in excess, the non-resident may claim a refund within five years of the payment date supported by the TRC and the ETA relief certificate. Where no comprehensive DTA applies, such as for certain US-resident shareholders under the limited US-Egypt arrangement, the statutory 10% final withholding remains applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates on payments to non-residents are 20% for interest and 20% for royalties. General treaty positions commonly reduce interest to 10% and royalties to 10% to 15% upon TRC and beneficial-ownership confirmation. Software license fees and scanning-technology royalties paid to a foreign parent are therefore subject to Egyptian withholding unless exempt under an applicable treaty, and failure to withhold renders the expense non-deductible and exposes the LLC to collection liability.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Egyptian TP guidelines, a Local File is mandatory when controlled transactions with any single foreign related party exceed EGP 8,000,000 in a fiscal year; a Master File is required when aggregate controlled transactions exceed EGP 40,000,000; Country-by-Country reporting applies where the multinational group consolidated revenue is at least EGP 12,000,000,000. A TP disclosure annex must be filed with the annual CIT return even below the documentation thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the ETA applies a substance-over-form anti-abuse principle under Article 30 of Income Tax Law No. 91/2005, a beneficial-ownership test for treaty relief, reinforced AML KYC requirements, and TP documentation rules. A mail-scanning CMRA must maintain licensed premises, engaged local staff, actual client contracts, an operational bank account, and independent decision-making records; a letterbox-only arrangement without staff or local management is exposed to denial of tax clearance, treaty benefits, and commercial-registration revocation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to file the annual CIT return, under-invoicing Stripe card-rail revenue, suppressing mail-scanning subscriptions, fabricating deductible invoices, or concealing dividend distributions to foreign shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax of 2% per month on unpaid amounts, penal assessment of 100% to 200% of the evaded tax, criminal fines up to EGP 1,000,000, and imprisonment of up to five years under Law No. 91/2005 as amended by Law No. 51/2023; assets and bank accounts may be attached by the Egyptian Tax Authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who certified false accounts are jointly and severally liable for unpaid CIT; enforcement courts may issue travel bans, freeze personal bank accounts, and place names on the police blacklist under Law No. 25/1996, with imprisonment imposed on officers who engineered fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a mailbox-only virtual office with no licensed staff, no genuine mail-scanning contracts, no operational records, and no economic substance, particularly when used as a letterbox for networks of shelf companies or nominee-controlled vehicles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commercial Registry and Investment Authority may dissolve the LLC, cancel its establishment license, and liquidate its assets; the ETA may re-assess taxable profits on a deemed-turnover basis and impose the 22.5% CIT with 2% monthly surcharges; fictitious-company provisions of Companies Law No. 159/1981 permit nullification of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil when the LLC is used as a cover: directors become personally liable for unpaid tax and third-party debts, may be sequestrated or declared bankrupt, and travel bans and asset freezes are routinely issued under the civil enforcement regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting corporate-registration mail, board resolutions, or payment forwarding for shell clients with concealed ultimate beneficial owners, or processing Stripe recurring payments for front companies that launder proceeds of tax evasion or other criminal activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Egyptian AML Law No. 80/2002 as amended by Law No. 8/2015 imposes imprisonment of up to 15 years and fines of up to EGP 5,000,000 for money laundering participation; FIU Egypt may freeze assets, the CMRA license is subject to administrative suspension, and the ETA may coordinate criminal seizure of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign hosting agreements, approve KYC bypasses, or fail to submit required reporting and suspicious-transaction reports bear criminal liability jointly with the LLC and are exposed to travel bans, personal account freezes, and prolonged investigation detention.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, software royalties, or scanning-technology license fees to the foreign parent, or failing to prepare the Local File and TP disclosure annex when related-party transactions exceed the EGP 8,000,000 threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may adjust taxable income to an arm's-length result, apply the 22.5% CIT on the adjustment, add 2% monthly delay surcharges, and impose documentation penalties under the Egyptian TP regulations; the assessment period is extended for non-disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general manager who signed inflated intercompany invoices may be made personally liable for the resulting tax deficiency under the doctrine of corporate waste; repeated TP misstatements additionally expose directors to criminal referrals for false bookkeeping.
